takeaway: Pouch nerves: first, trigeminal (V); second, facial (VII); third, glossopharyngeal (IX); fourth and sixth, branches of the vagus (X).

lines.text: Which nerve innervates the second pharyngeal pouch?
The second pharyngeal pouch is innervated
by the facial nerve, cranial nerve seven.
The first pouch has the trigeminal nerve, cranial nerve five.
The third pouch has the glossopharyngeal nerve, cranial nerve nine.
The fourth and sixth have branches of the vagus nerve, cranial nerve ten.
So the answer is the facial nerve.
